events.text:
It is 7:00 at Valley Parts, where two refrigerated trucks arrive at the same time with shipments scheduled for receiving. Only one dock door has a working seal, and one driver is close to his hours-of-service limit and wants to drop the trailer and go.
Choices: Decide on the spot: unload the driver near his hours limit first and tell the other carrier to wait 40 minutes. | Call both carriers' dispatchers, lay out the constraint, and let them agree on an order before anything moves. | Hold both trucks until maintenance confirms whether the other dock door's seal can be patched safely.
events.title: Two trucks, one dock door

events.text:
At Valley Parts, Darnell's cycle count shows 14 pallets of inventory missing from a lane the system says is full. A customer pickup for those pallets is scheduled at noon. Nobody has touched the lane since the night shift.
Choices: Walk the lane yourself with Darnell, pallet by pallet, before telling the customer anything. | Call the customer now, explain there may be a shortfall, and offer to substitute from another lot. | Ask Tou to pull the night shift scanner logs while you start building the order from overflow stock.
events.title: The count is off

events.text:
The dock thermometer at Valley Parts reads 104°F, and the afternoon is forecast to get hotter. Two temps in their first week are skipping water breaks to keep up with the line rate you set this morning.
Choices: Cut the line rate for the afternoon and enforce a shade break every hour, even if outbound slips. | Keep the rate but pair each new temp with a veteran who will make sure they take breaks. | Talk to the two temps quietly yourself, then check on them every 30 minutes.
events.title: Heat on the dock
